newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOCUS-Anglo holds profits despite bullion.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Anglo holds profits despite bullion.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said on Thursday its June quarter gold results were financially good and reasonable in operational terms, despite the current weak bullion price.

But Bobby Godsell, chief executive of Anglogold, the group's gold division, said costs at Vaal Reefs Exploration and Mining Co were unsustainable at current output levels and the low gold price necessitated a review of all marginal shafts at Free State Consolidated Gold Mines Ltd -- the world's largest gold mine.

"In the context of a weak, and indeed weakening, gold price, the financial results reported today are good. In operational terms, the results presented today are reasonable," Godsell told a results presentation.
Anglogold announced that available profits from its gold mines in the three months to end-June fell to 220.7 million rand ($48.4 million), down two percent on the previous March quarter.
"In operational terms, the results presented today are reasonable. Western Deep Levels and Ergo had excellent quarters. Concerns continue about Vaal Reefs and Freegold," Godsell said.

Although Vaal Reefs increased gold output to 16,641 kg from 16,022 kg, Godsell said the mine was taking longer than expected to move on to its new working calendar, with some employees at the mine's key long-life shafts -- Nos 8,9 and 10 -- resisting the calendar's implementation.
"The recent industry wage and productivity agreement will hopefully break the logjam," he said.
Vaal Reefs' available profit for the quarter fell to 70.5 million rand from 77.3 million rand.
"In general, present cost structures are unsustainable for present levels of production," Godsell said, adding that the mine's key No 8 shaft had a poor quarter.
Turning to Freegold, Godsell detailed the fate of the five shafts identified as marginal at the end of the March quarter.
He said Western Holdings No 2 shaft was closed during the June quarter and Western Holdings No 3 shaft would be closed within the next three to six months.

"The underlying tension is between the planned reduction in unprofitable production and the continuing level of costs," Godsell said. Freegold has stated it intends bringing its production closer to sustainable levels.

Certain unpayable sections of Freddies No 5 shaft were closed and performance had improved Godsell said. But he added that similar measures at president Steyn Nos 2 and 5 shafts were less successful and further remedial action would be taken.
"The low gold price necessitates a review of all marginal shafts and stakeholders will be advised of any decisions emanating from this," Anglogold said.
Freegold's second quarter available profit fell to 56.8 million rand from 62.9 million rand previously. It's gold output dropped to 18,155 kg from 19,195 kg.
Freegold mine manager Dave Hodgson said the mine's longlife shafts improved their production by 123 kg but that this was not enough to offset the poor performance of the other shafts.
Hodgson said Freegold would continue with its planned downsizing because the ore reserves in many of the old shafts were coming to the end of their lives.

Capital expenditure at Freegold is expected to be cut back to 137 million rand for the financial year and management said that it was mindful that any further cutbacks could have a negative impact in the long-term.
